item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning no. Xi’s 2024 record contains repeated people-centered language and some real welfare policy, but the strongest independent evidence says welfare was still secondary to Party control, censorship, and repression.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Xi urges promotion of high-quality and sufficient employment | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-05-29 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202405/29/content_WS6657333ac6d0868f4e8e79f2.html) | Xi called employment the “new orientation and mission” and tied it to people-centered development and workers’ fulfillment, happiness, and security. | 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10 |
| Yes | Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Further Deepening Reform Comprehensively to Advance Chinese Modernization | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-21 | [page](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xw/zyxw/202407/t20240721_11457437.html) | The plenum resolution says improving people’s quality of life, social fairness, and wellbeing are “ultimate objectives,” and it names jobs, income distribution, social security, and public services as priorities. | 6B.1, 5B.10 |
| Yes | China's No.1 central document for 2024 charts roadmap for rural revitalization | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-02-03 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202402/03/content_WS65be363cc6d0868f4e8e3c18.html) | The annual policy blueprint prioritizes food security, preventing relapse into poverty, rural industry, and income growth, which is concrete welfare-oriented policy. | 6B.1, 5B.10 |
| Yes | China creates 2.45 million jobs through work-relief programs | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-11-04 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202411/04/content_WS672879d6c6d0868f4e8ec91e.html) | Local work-relief programs created 2.45 million jobs for low-income workers in the first three quarters of 2024 and paid 31 billion yuan in wages. | 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10 |
| No | China: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [page](https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House says the CCP tightly controls state, media, online speech, universities, business, and civil society, which points to control rather than welfare as the governing priority. | 6B.1 |
| No | World Report 2024: China | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | [page](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/china) | HRW says Xinjiang abuses amount to crimes against humanity, with mass detention and forced assimilation, and notes Xi called the policy a “success.” | 6B.1 |
| No | China attempts to ‘gaslight’ international community at UN human rights review | Amnesty International | 2024-01-23 | [page](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/01/china-attempts-to-gaslight-international-community-at-un-human-rights-review/) | Amnesty says China denied the scope of abuses and repackaged repression in Xinjiang and Hong Kong as stability, which looks like propaganda rather than welfare-first governance. | 6B.1 |
| No | China: Overseas students face harassment and surveillance in campaign of transnational repression | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | [page](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/china-overseas-students-face-harassment-and-surveillance-in-campaign-of-transnational-repression/) | Amnesty reports Chinese and Hong Kong students abroad were photographed, followed, and pressured through family members to silence activism, showing coercive control over people’s lives. | 6B.1 |

**Search gap**
- The affirmative case is mostly official rhetoric and state policy output, not an independent test of priority under tradeoffs.
- I did not find a 2024 source that directly shows Xi choosing welfare over propaganda, Party control, or repression when those goals conflicted.
- The independent record is broad and consistent on repression, so the welfare-first claim is only partially supported and looks instrumental rather than foundational.
